fact_text: The analyst stresses operating leverage: if a product sells at 100 with 95 of cost, profit is 5, so a small price rise plus a small cost fall can multiply profit several times and lift the share with it.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HALEON - Pharma Sector - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistani pharma raw materials (APIs) are largely oil derivatives, so falling crude prices cut pharma production costs.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HALEON - Pharma Sector - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst attributes a 300-500% jump in Pakistani pharma profits to three combined developments: cheaper oil-linked raw materials, deregulated non-essential medicine prices rising 10-15%, and a period with no rupee devaluation.
period: the two years before the video
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HALEON - Pharma Sector - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistan follows a World Bank-style split of medicines into essential and non-essential; if even one active ingredient in a formulation is non-essential, the whole medicine is classed non-essential and its price is deregulated.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HALEON - Pharma Sector - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Non-essential medicines in Pakistan have deregulated prices, letting a company set its own price, while essential medicines only get administratively allowed increases.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HALEON - Pharma Sector - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Because Pakistani pharma firms import APIs and only convert them into finished medicine, their plants are relatively cheap, giving the sector a generally high return on invested capital.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HALEON - Pharma Sector - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Multinational pharma subsidiaries in Pakistan get raw material from their foreign principals on two to three months of credit, so they can launch or scale products with almost no working-capital outlay.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HALEON - Pharma Sector - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: With non-essential medicine prices deregulated, the analyst expects multinationals to keep importing products from their global portfolios into Pakistan at prices of their own choosing.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HALEON - Pharma Sector - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: To track Pakistani pharma, the analyst monitors product prices, raw-material costs and import duties, and the pipeline of new product launches, since small moves in each swing profits sharply.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HALEON - Pharma Sector - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Haleon Pakistan's core volume product is the Panadol paracetamol tablet, a very low-priced mass consumer medicine, alongside consumer health brands it launches from its global portfolio.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HALEON - Pharma Sector - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst links an almost five-fold rise in Haleon Pakistan's profit versus the prior year to a Panadol tablet price moving from about PKR 3.16 to about PKR 3.5 while paracetamol input cost fell.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HALEON - Pharma Sector - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: On a roughly PKR 3.5 retail Panadol tablet, Haleon Pakistan sells to the distributor at about PKR 2.5-3.5 against production cost of roughly PKR 1.5-2.5, leaving about PKR 1 of profit per tablet.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HALEON - Pharma Sector - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: New Panadol variants such as Extra, Ultra and Night fall in the deregulated non-essential class and sell near PKR 10 per tablet, so the analyst estimates per-tablet profit of roughly PKR 4-5, far above plain Panadol.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HALEON - Pharma Sector - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst argues new high-margin Panadol variants could lift Haleon Pakistan's total profit substantially even while contributing only 5-10% of sales within a few years, because profit per tablet is several times higher.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HALEON - Pharma Sector - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Haleon Pakistan does not manufacture Panadol itself but has it toll-manufactured by third parties including GSK and Pharmatec, so insourcing production removes a toll fee.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HALEON - Pharma Sector - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Haleon Pakistan is building a Panadol plant at Jamshoro using direct-compression technology with capacity near 9 billion tablets a year, at a stated cost of roughly USD 12-15 million.
period: project announced for 2025, completion within about a year
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HALEON - Pharma Sector - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst estimates the Panadol insourcing project costs about PKR 4 billion and saves roughly PKR 1.5-2 billion a year pre-tax (about PKR 1 billion after tax), an ROIC near 25% from cost savings alone before any demand or export upside.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HALEON - Pharma Sector - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Haleon Pakistan's stated launch pipeline includes the Centrum multivitamin, new Panadol versions and the Robitussin cough medicine, with other global brands possible later.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HALEON - Pharma Sector - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Under a five-year policy to cut raw-material duties, pharma raw-material duties fell about 2-3% on average, with a 3-4% price increase on essential medicines allowed the following year.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HALEON - Pharma Sector - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst treats a negative cash cycle (cash collected from customers before suppliers are paid) as a hallmark of durable businesses, since it funds scaling internally and most failures come from cash flow, not margins.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Get Paid Before You Pay: How Smart Businesses Fund Themselves' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A primary surplus is federal revenue minus all expenditure except interest costs; with interest near inflation, a primary surplus plus 2-3% GDP growth lowers debt-to-GDP over time.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TOP 4 MACRO INDICATORS FOR INVESTING IN PSX' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's first indicator is the primary balance: when Pakistan runs a primary surplus or small primary deficit, fiscal discipline raises confidence and investors award listed companies higher PE multiples.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TOP 4 MACRO INDICATORS FOR INVESTING IN PSX' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Historically Pakistan has achieved a primary surplus or near balance only while inside an IMF programme, so the analyst sees the programme's main value as imposed fiscal discipline rather than the dollar loans themselves, which then unlocks other lenders.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TOP 4 MACRO INDICATORS FOR INVESTING IN PSX' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Interest rates hit share prices through three channels: cyclical demand and capacity utilisation affecting gross margins, the company's own finance cost, and the discounting of future earnings into present value.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TOP 4 MACRO INDICATORS FOR INVESTING IN PSX' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Shiller's rule puts a market's fair PE at 20 minus long-term interest rates, but the analyst finds that in Pakistan 20 minus the CURRENT policy rate fits the last 20 years of data better.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TOP 4 MACRO INDICATORS FOR INVESTING IN PSX' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Oil was about 15% of Pakistan's import bill in 2000-2010, whereas oil plus oil-linked LNG now make up roughly 25-30%, so oil price spikes now threaten macro stability far more.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TOP 4 MACRO INDICATORS FOR INVESTING IN PSX' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Rising oil once lifted the PSX because OGDC and PPL were about 30% of the KSE-100 and gained from higher prices; their weight is now only 7-8% and they carry circular-debt problems, so higher oil is now net negative for the index.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TOP 4 MACRO INDICATORS FOR INVESTING IN PSX' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A widening current account deficit drains FX reserves, and when reserves fall to single digits default fears compress market multiples, so a company earning PKR 1 that once fetched PKR 6-7 of price may only fetch PKR 3-4.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TOP 4 MACRO INDICATORS FOR INVESTING IN PSX' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Contrary to the common belief that IMF programmes raise rates, the analyst says the data show Pakistani interest rates begin falling within six to twelve months of entering a programme.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TOP 4 MACRO INDICATORS FOR INVESTING IN PSX' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's combined rule: a depressed market plus high primary and current account deficits plus a fresh IMF agreement is a favourable entry setup, because surplus, deficit narrowing and rate cuts usually follow within a few quarters.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TOP 4 MACRO INDICATORS FOR INVESTING IN PSX' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Splitting 25 years of PSX returns into five-year blocks shows the bulk of all returns came in just two of those blocks, where savings would have roughly quadrupled, which is why the analyst focuses on timing boom and bust cycles.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TOP 4 MACRO INDICATORS FOR INVESTING IN PSX' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst sorts PSX ideas into six investing themes, including cyclicals (autos, cement, steel), stalwarts (international FMCG), slow growers (urea/fertiliser) and hedges, and uses the theme to set the risk-reward and position size.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TOP INVESTING THEMES - INVEST LIKE A PRO | FOR ALL RETAIL INVESTORS' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: North-based Pakistani cement plants are naturally protected from imports because cement cannot travel economically, so unlike steel they do not permanently lose earning power to cheap imports.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TOP INVESTING THEMES - INVEST LIKE A PRO | FOR ALL RETAIL INVESTORS' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistan's steel industry illustrates permanent loss of earning power: cheap imports through the Fata/Pata route force producers to sacrifice margins and lose market share, so a cheap-looking valuation can be a trap.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TOP INVESTING THEMES - INVEST LIKE A PRO | FOR ALL RETAIL INVESTORS' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's rules for cyclicals: cap them at 25% of the portfolio and only when trading below 40% of fair value (15% if the discount is smaller), and never buy a highly leveraged cyclical since it may not survive the down-cycle.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TOP INVESTING THEMES - INVEST LIKE A PRO | FOR ALL RETAIL INVESTORS' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: When assessing a cyclical, the analyst first asks how protected the industry is from imports, because a globally cheap product with low Pakistani duties can destroy a company's earning power permanently.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TOP INVESTING THEMES - INVEST LIKE A PRO | FOR ALL RETAIL INVESTORS' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst classifies Pakistani banks as cyclicals because of sovereign exposure: a bank with PKR 100 billion book value holding PKR 1,000 billion of government bonds would lose about PKR 75 billion of book value after tax from a 15% haircut.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TOP INVESTING THEMES - INVEST LIKE A PRO | FOR ALL RETAIL INVESTORS' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistani banks were very cheap in 2023 when debt-to-GDP near 80% raised real debt-restructuring risk; with it around 70% and an IMF programme in place that risk has been priced out, but banks would act cyclically again if debt-to-GDP neared 80% and the programme derailed.
period: 2023 versus the time of the video
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TOP INVESTING THEMES - INVEST LIKE A PRO | FOR ALL RETAIL INVESTORS' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's valuation rule is to pay more than a 10x PE only when the business earns above 40% ROIC, and considers sector-standard PE norms meaningless since Pakistani FMCG traded at 5-7x in 2005-2006 during a bull market.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TOP INVESTING THEMES - INVEST LIKE A PRO | FOR ALL RETAIL INVESTORS' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst warns that buying above a 20x PE can give zero return even if profits double in three to four years, because the multiple can halve; a high price turns a good company into a bad investment.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TOP INVESTING THEMES - INVEST LIKE A PRO | FOR ALL RETAIL INVESTORS' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst treats Pakistan's urea producers as slow growers whose business economics keep profits secure through almost any domestic shock, but notes gas price changes can still swing individual companies' earnings sharply.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TOP INVESTING THEMES - INVEST LIKE A PRO | FOR ALL RETAIL INVESTORS' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Buying dollar-revenue exporters as a devaluation hedge can fail: devaluation does raise their profits, but the macro uncertainty behind it compresses every company's PE, so overall savings can still fall.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TOP INVESTING THEMES - INVEST LIKE A PRO | FOR ALL RETAIL INVESTORS' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Because many PSX companies trade well below their real value, the analyst treats a buyout or a move to delisting as a value-unlocking event for minority holders.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TOP INVESTING THEMES - INVEST LIKE A PRO | FOR ALL RETAIL INVESTORS' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: After a Bangladesh airport fire halted hydrogen peroxide imports, the next-best source was Korea at about USD 800 per ton versus Bangladesh's USD 400, so this local producer's per-ton earnings jumped from roughly USD 50-100 to about USD 400.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TOP INVESTING THEMES - INVEST LIKE A PRO | FOR ALL RETAIL INVESTORS' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A local chemical producer's margin is set by the landed cost of the cheapest available import, so losing the cheapest import source raises domestic realised prices to the next-best origin's price.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TOP INVESTING THEMES - INVEST LIKE A PRO | FOR ALL RETAIL INVESTORS' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's core ratio is future ROIC, the return a business would earn on an extra PKR 100 invested; he argues a business with about 30% future ROIC tends to deliver a similar long-run share-price CAGR.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HOW MANY STOCKS YOU SHOULD HAVE IN YOUR PORTFOLIO TO MAXIMIZE PROFITS?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst ranks holdings by future ROIC and allocates about 13-15% each to the top three ideas and 10-12% each to the next five, never exceeding 15% in a single company.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HOW MANY STOCKS YOU SHOULD HAVE IN YOUR PORTFOLIO TO MAXIMIZE PROFITS?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst recommends seven to eight stocks when over half of savings are in equities and no more than five when under a quarter is, arguing each extra name dilutes the average return (Lynch's 'diworsification').
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HOW MANY STOCKS YOU SHOULD HAVE IN YOUR PORTFOLIO TO MAXIMIZE PROFITS?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Minority shareholders cannot control when the market recognises fair value, so the analyst holds seven to eight names to avoid the stress of a portfolio stalling while the index rises.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HOW MANY STOCKS YOU SHOULD HAVE IN YOUR PORTFOLIO TO MAXIMIZE PROFITS?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Frequent portfolio churn in Pakistan costs trading fees and capital gains tax, while the tax owed falls the longer a stock is held, so the analyst favours letting winners run.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'HOW MANY STOCKS YOU SHOULD HAVE IN YOUR PORTFOLIO TO MAXIMIZE PROFITS?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In the PSX bull market of the past two to three years, each rally has been followed by a profit-taking correction of roughly 10-12% from the peak, or about 25-30% of the most recent up-leg.
period: the two to three years to February of the video
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX Crashing! What to expect NOW?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst lists the triggers of successive PSX corrections: the February 2024 election uncertainty (65,000 to about 56-57,000), a Supreme Court change in Sep-Oct 2024 (85,000 to about 78,000), the Trump-election and Pakistan-India conflict period, and later foreign selling.
period: July 2023 to February of the video
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX Crashing! What to expect NOW?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Foreign portfolio investors are now a small share of PSX ownership while domestic mutual funds' equity holdings have grown, so local funds and high-net-worth individuals absorb foreign selling with limited index damage.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX Crashing! What to expect NOW?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Global shocks such as tariff announcements cut both ways for Pakistan: a slowing world economy makes imported commodities cheaper, which helps Pakistan, but foreign investors sell frontier markets and move to US bonds in a flight to safety.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX Crashing! What to expect NOW?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst distinguishes two ways markets test investors: a sharp fast drop, which he expects to end in a V-shaped recovery, and a long sideways drift such as January to May 2025, which tests conviction through time.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX Crashing! What to expect NOW?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst judged equities still the best Pakistani asset class during the correction because deposit rates had fallen with low interest rates and are taxed, while real estate remained inactive.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX Crashing! What to expect NOW?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A PSX company stays Shariah-compliant only if non-compliant income is under 5% of total revenue, so a compliant company can still earn a small share of non-compliant income.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'The Dividend Purification Problem Every Muslim Investor Faces' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The PSX KMI All Share index is recomposed twice a year, in May and November, and the published list shows each company's non-compliant-income ratio plus which names were added or dropped and why.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'The Dividend Purification Problem Every Muslim Investor Faces' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Dividend purification means giving away the share of a dividend matching the company's non-compliant income ratio: the cap is 5% but published ratios are often far lower, so the actual amount can be a fraction of a percent or nil.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'The Dividend Purification Problem Every Muslim Investor Faces' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Official SECP and PSX guidance requires no purification of capital gains on a Shariah-compliant stock, on the reasoning that a share price moves for many reasons beyond the company's income.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'The Dividend Purification Problem Every Muslim Investor Faces' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Over the 25 years from 1999 the analyst puts nominal Pakistani returns at about 66x for equities, 40x for gold, 20-40x for real estate, 12x for fixed income and only 5.5x for holding US dollars.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Investing in Pakistan Stock Exchange is Super Risky?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistani fixed-income returns broadly track inflation because the State Bank's policy rate is set largely in line with inflation, so savers should expect little real return.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Investing in Pakistan Stock Exchange is Super Risky?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Gold's large PKR return comes from two stacked drivers: the dollar ounce price rising and the rupee depreciating, which is why the analyst views gold as a reasonable hedge against devaluation.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Investing in Pakistan Stock Exchange is Super Risky?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistani fixed-income investors typically face a 15% tax rate, equity and property gains are taxed from 15% down to 0% after six years of holding, trading fees are about 0.2% on equities versus 3-5% all-in on property and 1-2% on gold.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Investing in Pakistan Stock Exchange is Super Risky?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistani real estate operates in a largely undocumented economy with no average price index, so returns are only visible through individual success stories like DHA Phase 6 Lahore rather than any market average.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Investing in Pakistan Stock Exchange is Super Risky?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Returns in Pakistani real estate come mainly from plot price appreciation, since building and renting a house yields only about 3-4%, and sometimes 1-2%.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Investing in Pakistan Stock Exchange is Super Risky?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst calls comparing one property scheme with the whole stock index flawed, since individual listed companies have returned 100x or more while the index average was 66x over 25 years.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Investing in Pakistan Stock Exchange is Super Risky?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst frames the PSX as a way to become an equal partner of Pakistan's leading business groups, naming Dawood (Engro), Nishat (Mian Mansha), Lucky (Muhammad Ali Tabba) and Meezan Bank's Kuwaiti shareholders.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Investing in Pakistan Stock Exchange is Super Risky?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Structurally, PSX investing needs only a few hundred or thousand rupees and is divisible and liquid, while Pakistani property needs millions, cannot be sold in parts, can take weeks or years to sell and carries developer-fraud risk.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Property Scams vs Stock Market: Where Is Your Money Actually Safe?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The common Pakistani property scam works through files sold before a society is built, with possession promised in two to five years, during which developers may abscond or deliver possession to only some file holders.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Property Scams vs Stock Market: Where Is Your Money Actually Safe?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Using the price history since 1997, the analyst cites Sazgar's share-price-only return of about 1,825x as evidence that top PSX outcomes exceed even the best-quoted real-estate examples, alongside Mari Petroleum and Meezan Bank.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Property Scams vs Stock Market: Where Is Your Money Actually Safe?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst argues that speculative plot buying has made Pakistani real estate far larger than the stock market and homes unaffordable, whereas equity investment funds company expansion and jobs.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Property Scams vs Stock Market: Where Is Your Money Actually Safe?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistani investors may only open accounts with SECP- and PSX-registered brokers and must pay by crossed cheque into the broking company's own bank account, never in cash or to a third-party account.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan Stock Market is a Scam? 4 Common Frauds & How to Protect Your Investments' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A CDC Investor Account gives a PSX investor direct custody of shares, protecting them if a broker defaults; shares can be transferred in after the two-day settlement, with a nominal transfer fee of roughly 0.004%.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan Stock Market is a Scam? 4 Common Frauds & How to Protect Your Investments' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Share price level says nothing about value: a PKR 5 share with 10 billion shares is a PKR 50 billion company, while a PKR 1,000 share with 10 million shares is far smaller, so market capitalisation is what matters.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan Stock Market is a Scam? 4 Common Frauds & How to Protect Your Investments' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's five-minute risk screen for a small PSX company checks total liabilities and bank debt, whether the auditor is a reputable firm, and whether any dividend was paid in the last five years.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan Stock Market is a Scam? 4 Common Frauds & How to Protect Your Investments' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Since even sound companies can fall 30-50% in a market downturn with no business fault, the analyst reviews each holding's quarterly report every three months and checks the market's PE before investing.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan Stock Market is a Scam? 4 Common Frauds & How to Protect Your Investments' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst cites the US 'lost decade', with the S&P 500 at the same level in 2012 as in 2000 despite an 8% average annual dollar return, to show long flat stretches are normal in equities.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan Stock Market is a Scam? 4 Common Frauds & How to Protect Your Investments' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst notes FFC's share only re-rated after the gas price differential between fertiliser producers emerged in 2024, when it outperformed a KSE-100 that rose about 80%.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN Financials at Young Entrepreneur Fest | Value Investing & Stock Market Quiz' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In the quiz the analyst takes the KSE-100's calendar-year gain as about 50% in 2023 and about 80% in 2024.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN Financials at Young Entrepreneur Fest | Value Investing & Stock Market Quiz' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst recalls Hubco's power purchase contracts being terminated around the end of 2024, which he treats as the reason the stock did not outperform in that period.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN Financials at Young Entrepreneur Fest | Value Investing & Stock Market Quiz' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst uses earnings yield as the reciprocal of the PE, so a share trading at a PE of 10 has a 10% earnings yield.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN Financials at Young Entrepreneur Fest | Value Investing & Stock Market Quiz' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst works with roughly 17% a year as the long-run profit growth available from listed Pakistani businesses when illustrating long-term compounding.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN Financials at Young Entrepreneur Fest | Value Investing & Stock Market Quiz' (YouTube transcript, undated)
